comparator.name: Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC degree includes 60 EC of introductory courses, 80 EC of later compulsory courses, a 15 EC internal minor, 15 EC of electives and two final assignments worth 5 EC each. This example uses the legal aid clinic and the public law essay.
components: Introduction to the Law of Obligations
Family Law and the Law of Persons

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Legal foundations, sources, interpretation, argument, rights and justice
Law in social, historical and economic context
Private, criminal, constitutional and administrative legal foundations
European Union and public international law
Legal research, writing, case analysis, advocacy and independent work
adjacent: Private law, obligations, property and civil disputes
Criminal law, criminal justice and public enforcement
Legal philosophy, ethics and theories of justice
Business, employment, social-security and commercial legal relationships
Employment, social security and public economic regulation
questions: How can rights, rules and legal reasoning resolve disputes and protect citizens?
How do constitutional, administrative, European and international institutions constrain public power?
How does law structure private, employment and commercial relationships?

selection.assessment: The broad plan uses the full UCR law sequence. The other plans emphasize public institutions or private and commercial relationships. Open Universiteit adds sustained study of Dutch law, legal writing and practice, and a required legal essay.

alternatives.label: Law, Politics and Society
alternatives.labelReason: Explore legal reasoning, rights and justice through criminal, private, constitutional, international and EU law. Use politics, economics and sociology to understand how legal institutions work in society.
alternatives.concept: Explore legal reasoning, rights and justice through criminal, private, constitutional, international and EU law. Use politics, economics and sociology to understand how legal institutions work in society.
progression: Legal foundations precede criminal, private, constitutional, international and EU law. Research methods precede public economics and negotiation.

alternatives.label: Public, International and European Law
alternatives.labelReason: Study how law constrains public power at home and across borders. Combine constitutional, international and EU law with public policy, comparative politics, and the history and sociology of institutions.
alternatives.concept: Study how law constrains public power at home and across borders. Combine constitutional, international and EU law with public policy, comparative politics, and the history and sociology of institutions.
alternatives.distinctness: Study how law constrains public power at home and across borders. Combine constitutional, international and EU law with public policy, comparative politics, and the history and sociology of institutions. This plan and option 1 each have 5 courses unique to that plan.
progression: Legal foundations precede constitutional, international and EU law. Comparative politics, sociology and research methods prepare for public policy and advanced work on institutions.

alternatives.label: Private Law and Business
alternatives.labelReason: Explore how contracts, property and trade shape business relationships. Combine private and transnational business law with economics, finance, negotiation and the study of digital responsibility.
alternatives.concept: Explore how contracts, property and trade shape business relationships. Combine private and transnational business law with economics, finance, negotiation and the study of digital responsibility.
alternatives.distinctness: Explore how contracts, property and trade shape business relationships. Combine private and transnational business law with economics, finance, negotiation and the study of digital responsibility. This plan and option 1 each have 11 courses unique to that plan. This plan and option 2 each have 14 courses unique to that plan.
progression: Legal and business foundations prepare for private and transnational business law. Research methods precede negotiation and econometrics.

blocks: Both introduce legal systems, sources and reasoning. OU focuses on Dutch law.
OU develops legal writing through fundamental-rights cases. UCR studies human rights in a separate course.
OU examines philosophical questions about law. UCR develops ethical reasoning in a broader course.
OU requires written legal case analysis and oral pleading. UCR develops negotiation and communication in separate courses.
OU studies the historical development of law. UCR offers broader historical study.
Both examine treaties, jurisdiction and relations between states.
Both study constitutional powers and legal limits. UCR compares multiple systems.
Both study EU institutions, legal authority and its effects on national law.
OU introduces Dutch administrative law, including how decisions by public authorities can be challenged.
OU builds on the introductory course with further study of Dutch administrative law.
OU adds a second course on EU law after its introduction.
OU offers a second constitutional law course focused on the Dutch system.
OU continues international law beyond the introductory course.
OU continues its sequence in Dutch administrative law.
Both cover contractual obligations. UCR combines contract, property and tort law in one course.
Both examine criminal liability, defenses and punishment. OU teaches Dutch criminal law.
OU gives property law a dedicated course. UCR covers property within a broader private-law course.
OU teaches liability in a dedicated course. UCR includes tort law in its private-law course.
OU deepens contract law after the introductory obligations and property courses.
OU continues property law beyond the introduction.
OU offers a dedicated course in Dutch criminal procedure.
OU studies substantive Dutch criminal law beyond the introduction.
OU teaches how civil cases proceed through Dutch courts.
OU deepens the criminal law sequence through selected topics.
OU teaches Dutch family law and the legal status of persons.
OU teaches Dutch company law. UCR studies transnational trade and commercial contracts.
OU studies law and technology. UCR examines AI fairness, privacy and responsibility in a separate course.
OU teaches legal writing using Dutch legal sources. UCR develops academic writing and argument across disciplines.
OU requires a 5 EC legal essay. This example uses public law. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose 15 EC of eligible electives or an external minor.
This example uses the supervised legal aid clinic. OU also offers internal minors in entrepreneurship and public enforcement.

notes.text: OU’s Dutch-taught LLB develops Dutch legal doctrine and practice alongside EU and international law. UCR combines selected areas of law with social science and humanities.

Dedicated study of Dutch administrative law, civil and criminal procedure, legal drafting and courtroom advocacy requires a law curriculum such as OU’s. The legal aid clinic shown here is one of OU’s internal minor choices.

audience.programmeDescription: This Dutch-taught, part-time Bachelor of Laws covers Dutch, European and international law. It develops legal analysis, writing and advocacy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options emphasize broad legal and social inquiry, public and international institutions, or private law and business. OU provides more depth in Dutch law and includes required legal writing and advocacy.
